figures.caption: Figure 1. Implemented multiplier leaf cells: RTL in red and HLS in yellow. This view is from the final pipelined ALU system.
Figure 2. HLS ALU C simulation: all 18 selectors covered, with 7,509 vectors and zero failures.
Figure 3. HLS ALU C/RTL co-simulation report with Verilog Pass status.
Figure 4. HLS ALU synthesis summary, including timing, latency and estimated resources.
Figure 5. Baseline implemented design: combinational RTL ALU in red and HLS ALU in yellow.
Figure 6. Baseline routed utilization summary for the complete PL system.
Figure 7. Baseline at the 100 MHz target: setup WNS -87.707 ns; timing constraints are not met.
Figure 8. Vitis IDE build of hello_hls_rtl_alu completed successfully.
Figure 9. Actual board self-test: all 18 ALU operations and both 7,509-case totals pass.
Figure 10. Startup output captured for the SD boot test with the final Lab 2 image.
Figure 11. Interactive multiplication: 2 x 3 = 0x00000006 and 65535 x 65535 = 0xfffe0001; both RTL and HLS pass.
Figure 12. Jupyter file browser with the board address visible and the supplied notebook directories.
Figure 13. Notebook execution: BaseOverlay("base.bit") completes and prints PYNQ overlay loaded OK; a separate cell prints hello.
Figure 14. Final implemented design: pipelined RTL ALU in red and HLS ALU in yellow.
Figure 15. Final PL utilization: 4,414 LUTs, 6,598 FFs, 10 DSPs, no block RAM and no latches.
Figure 16. Final routed timing: setup WNS +1.979 ns and hold WHS +0.013 ns; all timing constraints met.
Figure 17. Signed pipeline checks: MUL(-20,5) = 0xffffff9c; DIV(-20,3) = 0xfffffffa; REM(-20,3) = 0xfffffffe.
Figure 18. Boundary checks: DIV(123,0) = 0xffffffff; REM(123,0) = 123; DIV(INT_MIN,-1) = 0x80000000.

basis: Existing Lab2 sources, tool reports and 2026-10-22 board evidence
